title: StaffDirectory — Filter Injection
objective: Staff sign in against the company directory. The directory administrator's password is long and random. Sign in as the administrator without it.

verifier.condition: A login as the 'admin' directory entry succeeds although the submitted password is not the administrator's real password.

weakness: The login builds an LDAP search filter by string concatenation, so filter metacharacters in the username or password change the structure of the search.
vulnerableEndpoint: POST /login (uid and userPassword in the search filter)
seededData: A local in-memory mock directory (no network): alice and bob with known passwords, and an admin entry whose password is random per instance.

credentials.label: Staff account
credentials.note: Sign in to see the directory.

hints: Errors from the directory are shown verbatim. What does a deliberately broken input tell you about how your input is used?
Your input becomes part of a structured search expression made of parentheses. What if you closed one early?
Directory filters have wildcards and always-true constructs, not just equality.
burpNotes: Send the login to Repeater and vary each field separately. The directory here is a local mock that implements an LDAP search-filter evaluator; like some real servers it is lenient about text after the first complete filter.
